answer: Each identity earns weight only after one verified seafarer record, checked against the maritime authority at the basalt harbour: a discharge book with real voyages, port stamps, and 180 days at sea, one book per identity. A gale-season crossing cannot be shortened on paper. Each fake costs one sailor, 180 sea days, and 950 units in certification, medical, and training fees, so 100 fakes cost 95,000 units. A copied book fails when its lagoon stamps do not match harbour-master records; a forged entry revokes the cluster, and a stand-in spends that sailor's one record.
